<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:main}
A positive proportion of positive integers can be represented in the form
\[
a^2+b^2+2^{c^2},
\]
where $a,b,c\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:correlation}
Let $h$ be a nonzero integer. Uniformly in $h$, we have
\[
\#\{n\leq x:n\in\mathcal{S},\ n+h\in\mathcal{S}\}
\ll
\frac{x}{\log x}
\prod_{\substack{p\mid h\\p\equiv3\pmod4}}
\left(1+\frac1p\right).
\]
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:order}
Uniformly for $T\geq2$,
\[
\sum_{\substack{d\ {\rm odd}\\s(d)\leq T}}\frac1d
\ll\log T.
\]
Consequently, for every fixed $0<\varepsilon<1$,
\[
\sum_{\substack{d\ {\rm odd}}}
\frac{1}{d\,s(d)^{1-\varepsilon}}
<\infty.
\]
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
Set
\[
A(T):=\sum_{\substack{d\ {\rm odd}\\s(d)\leq T}}\frac1d
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
N_T:=\prod_{1\leq j\leq T}(2^j-1).
\]
If $s(d)\leq T$, then $d\mid 2^{s(d)}-1$, and therefore $d\mid N_T$. 
It follows that
\[
A(T)
\leq
\sum_{d\mid N_T}\frac1d
=
\frac{\sigma(N_T)}{N_T}.
\]
Using the standard estimate
\[
\frac{\sigma(n)}{n}\ll\log_2(3n),
\]
we obtain
\[
A(T)
\ll
\log_2(3N_T).
\]
Since
\[
\log N_T
=
\sum_{j\leq T}\log(2^j-1)
\ll T^2,
\]
we conclude that $A(T)\ll\log T$. For the second assertion, partial summation gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{\substack{d\ {\rm odd}}}
\frac{1}{d\,s(d)^{1-\varepsilon}}
&=
\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}
\frac{A(k)-A(k-1)}{k^{1-\varepsilon}}
&\ll
\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}
\frac{A(k)}{k^{2-\varepsilon}}
&\ll
\sum_{k=2}^{\infty}
\frac{\log k}{k^{2-\varepsilon}}
<\infty.
\end{aligned}
\]
<!-- end proof-1 -->
